title: How the ‘luteal uglies’ impact women during their periods
description:
Across social media young women are discussing the "luteal uglies." These are changes in appearance and mood that women experience during the luteal phase of their menstrual cycle. We hear from women in Vietnam, the Philippines, and the UK about the symptoms they experience, from acne and bloating to fatigue and brain fog.

But what’s behind these changes? Dr Helen O'Neill, an associate professor in reproductive and molecular genetics at University College London, explains how changing hormone levels impact women’s bodies and their brains. She also offers some tips and coping strategies.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討社群媒體熱議的「黃體期變醜」 luteal uglies 現象，即女性在月經來潮前約一週的黃體期所經歷的生理與心理變化。節目邀請多位女性分享痘痘、水腫、疲勞、情緒波動與腦霧等症狀，並由倫敦大學學院副教授 Helen O'Neill 博士解析背後的科學原理。她指出，黃體期時雌激素與黃體素濃度的急劇下降，會影響皮脂分泌、血清素活性與大腦功能。 O'Neill 博士亦提供實用應對策略，包含記錄月經週期、維持適度運動、改善睡眠衛生與避免飲酒，並強調男女皆應加強對月經週期的正確認知。
summaryEn: In this episode of BBC's What in the World, host Hannah Gelbart explores the viral social media phenomenon known as the "luteal uglies"—the physical and emotional changes women experience during the luteal phase, the week or so preceding their period. Listeners share common symptoms, including skin breakouts, bloating, fatigue, mood swings, and brain fog. Dr. Helen O'Neill, an associate professor in reproductive and molecular genetics at University College London, explains that rapid drops in estrogen and progesterone during this phase drive these shifts by affecting sebum production, serotonin activity, and brain function. Dr. O'Neill offers practical management strategies such as cycle tracking, light exercise, good sleep hygiene, and avoiding alcohol, while emphasizing the importance of educating both men and women about menstrual cycle health.
